title: Data Science
summary: In 20 weeks (5 months), students go from their first Python script to answering real business questions with data: cleaning messy datasets, writing SQL, running statistical tests and A/B tests, building dashboards, predicting and forecasting with ML, and presenting recommendations to decision-makers. Every project ends with a short written takeaway, because a data scientist's job is to help someone decide.
prerequisites: None. No prior coding or statistics required; Class 12 maths is enough.
audience: Undergraduate students from any branch. No prior coding or statistics required; Class 12 maths is enough.
format: Two 90-minute theory + live-coding sessions and one 3-hour lab each week (about 6 contact hours per week, ~120 hours total), plus 3-4 hours of self-study and project work.
teamSize: Weekly projects are individual; the Week 14 competition and the capstone are in teams of 2-4.
hardware: Any laptop with 8 GB RAM. Google Colab and Kaggle notebooks work as fallbacks.
outcome: A portfolio of 19 projects on GitHub / Kaggle, a public dashboard, and one capstone with a demo video.
learningOutcomes: Write clean Python and use Pandas and NumPy to clean, reshape and combine real-world data from files, APIs and websites.
Query and design relational databases with SQL, including joins, CTEs and window functions.
Visualise data clearly and build interactive dashboards for business users.
Apply descriptive and inferential statistics, hypothesis tests, A/B tests and regression analysis correctly.
Build, evaluate and explain ML models for prediction, segmentation, recommendation and time-series forecasting.
Analyse text data (including with LLMs) and process large datasets with PySpark.
Deploy a model or dashboard, check it for bias and privacy risks, and communicate findings to non-technical audiences.
highlights: Starts from zero: no prior coding or statistics required
19 portfolio projects plus a team capstone with demo video
Grading is 90% hands-on work, marked on analysis and communication
Runs on student laptops and free tiers; no paid software

phases.title: Python, data wrangling and SQL
phases.summary: Most of a data scientist's time goes into getting and cleaning data. This phase builds fluent Python and Pandas, data collection from APIs and websites, and two weeks of SQL, the tool used in almost every data job and interview.
phases.gate: Load raw data into a database, clean it, and answer business questions with SQL and Pandas.

phases.title: Visualisation, statistics and analytics
phases.summary: Students learn to explore data visually, tell real patterns from noise with statistics, design and analyse A/B tests, and present findings in dashboards and memos that decision-makers actually use.
phases.gate: Test a claim or experiment correctly and present results in a dashboard and a one-page memo.

phases.title: Machine learning and forecasting
phases.summary: Students build, validate and explain the models businesses ask for most: prices, churn and risk, customer segments, recommendations and demand forecasts, always compared against a simple baseline.
phases.gate: Build, validate and explain a predictive or forecasting model that beats a sensible baseline.

phases.title: Specialisation, production and capstone
phases.summary: Students analyse text (including with LLMs), process big data with PySpark, deploy models responsibly, and prepare for jobs while finishing the capstone.
phases.gate: Handle text and big data, deploy their work, and deliver a complete capstone.

weeks.title: Python basics
outcomes: Set up Python, Jupyter, Colab and Git.
Write programs with variables, conditionals, loops and functions.
Use AI coding assistants while understanding every line.
topics: Course intro: what data scientists do, with real case studies
Installing Python 3.12+, Jupyter, VS Code; Google Colab
weeks.lab: Pair-program a number-guessing game, then refactor it into functions. Push to GitHub.

project.title: Cricket scorecard analyser
project.brief: Reads ball-by-ball data for an innings and reports runs, strike rates, boundaries and top performers.
deliverables: At least 4 functions with clear names
Handles bad input lines without crashing
Summary printed as a neat table

weeks.title: Data structures, files, OOP and Git
outcomes: Choose the right data structure for a problem.
Read and write CSV and JSON files.
Model problems with classes and dataclasses.
weeks.lab: Build a contact book with add / search / delete saved to JSON.

project.title: Student records manager
project.brief: Add, search, update and summarise student records stored in CSV.
deliverables: Student modelled as a class or dataclass
project.stretch: Export a summary report to JSON.

weeks.title: NumPy and Pandas fundamentals
outcomes: Use NumPy arrays and vectorised operations.
Load, select, filter and transform data with Pandas.
Aggregate and combine tables.
topics: Pandas Series and DataFrames; loading CSV / Excel
pivot_table, apply, string and date methods
weeks.lab: Answer 10 guided questions on a sales dataset using only Pandas.

project.title: Movies / OTT titles analysis
project.brief: Answer 15 business questions about a streaming catalogue with Pandas.
deliverables: Questions cover filtering, grouping, merging and dates
Each answer shown as a table or number
Takeaway paragraph for a content team

weeks.title: Data cleaning and data collection
outcomes: Clean messy real-world data systematically.
Collect data from APIs and websites ethically.
Move analyst work from Excel to Python.
topics: Missing values, duplicates, wrong types, inconsistent text, outliers
Tidy data; melt and pivot; combining many files
Public APIs with requests; JSON to DataFrame
Web scraping with BeautifulSoup; robots.txt and ethics
Excel / Google Sheets for analysts: pivots, lookups; Excel vs Pandas
weeks.lab: Scrape a permitted public table (e.g. a Wikipedia list) and clean it into a DataFrame.

project.title: Messy-data clean-up
project.brief: Clean a deliberately messy real dataset (e.g. Indian real-estate listings) and publish a tidy version.
deliverables: Every cleaning step documented with reasons
Before / after quality checks (nulls, types, duplicates)
Clean file saved as CSV and Parquet
project.stretch: Write reusable cleaning functions with tests.

weeks.title: SQL fundamentals
outcomes: Explain tables, keys and relationships.
Filter, sort, aggregate and join data with SQL.
Translate business questions into queries.
topics: Relational databases, primary and foreign keys
SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, DISTINCT
CASE, NULL handling, LIKE, IN, BETWEEN
Aggregates: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX
weeks.lab: SQL drill: 20 guided queries on a college database, checked against expected results.

project.title: E-commerce query set
project.brief: Write 25 queries of increasing difficulty on an orders / customers / products database.
deliverables: Covers filters, aggregates, GROUP BY / HAVING and 5+ joins
Each query answers a stated business question
One-line explanation and output for each
project.stretch: Solve 20 extra problems on an online SQL practice platform.

weeks.title: Advanced SQL and SQL with Python
outcomes: Use subqueries, CTEs and window functions.
Design a simple normalised database.
Combine SQL and Pandas in one workflow.
topics: Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, running totals
When to use SQL vs Pandas
Analyst patterns: cohorts, retention, funnels, month-over-month growth
weeks.lab: Timed practical SQL test (graded), then build a funnel query together.

project.title: Retail sales analysis (Phase 1 project)
project.brief: Load raw CSVs into PostgreSQL and answer business questions with SQL and Pandas.
deliverables: Schema designed and loaded from raw CSVs
10 business questions answered, including a cohort retention table
At least 3 queries use CTEs or window functions
project.stretch: Automate the load with a Python script.

weeks.title: Visualisation and EDA
outcomes: Choose the right chart for a question.
Spot and fix misleading charts.
Run a structured exploratory analysis.
topics: Principles: chart choice, colour, labels, clutter
Misleading charts: truncated axes, dual axes, 3D
The EDA loop: questions -> charts -> insights
weeks.lab: Critique 10 real charts from the news in small groups.

project.title: Chart makeover + interactive EDA
project.brief: Redesign 5 bad charts, then build an interactive EDA of an Indian open dataset (e.g. state-wise air quality).
deliverables: Before / after for each makeover with reasons
Notebook published on Kaggle or GitHub
project.stretch: Add a choropleth map of India.

weeks.title: Descriptive statistics and probability
outcomes: Summarise data with the right statistics.
Reason with probability and conditional probability.
Recognise common distributions.
topics: Mean, median, mode; spread, IQR, percentiles, skew
Bayes' rule with real examples (medical tests, spam)
weeks.lab: Simulate the birthday problem and a medical-test false-positive scenario.

project.title: IPL player consistency report
project.brief: Rank batters and bowlers on consistency, not just averages, using descriptive statistics.
deliverables: At least 4 statistics used and justified
Consistency ranking with a clear method
project.stretch: Estimate win probability for common match situations.

weeks.title: Inferential statistics
outcomes: Explain sampling and the central limit theorem.
Build and interpret confidence intervals.
Run and interpret common hypothesis tests.
topics: Errors, power, statistical vs practical significance, p-hacking
weeks.lab: Bootstrap a confidence interval and compare with the formula.

project.title: Test five claims with data
project.brief: Test real claims (e.g. 'students with coaching score higher', 'weekend sales are higher').
deliverables: Correct test chosen and assumptions checked
Effect sizes and confidence intervals reported
project.stretch: Apply a multiple-testing correction and discuss the change.

weeks.title: A/B testing and regression analysis
outcomes: Design and analyse an A/B test.
Separate correlation from causation.
Fit and interpret regression models.
topics: Experiment design: metrics, randomisation, sample size, duration
Pitfalls: peeking, novelty effect, Simpson's paradox
Linear and multiple regression with statsmodels
Interpreting coefficients; dummy variables; checking residuals
weeks.lab: Calculate required sample sizes for three experiment scenarios.

project.title: A/B test and pricing analysis
project.brief: Analyse a website A/B test and estimate how price and discounts affect sales.
deliverables: Ship / don't ship recommendation with evidence
Memo written for a product manager
project.stretch: Check the A/B result separately for mobile and desktop users.

weeks.title: Dashboards, BI and data storytelling
outcomes: Design useful KPIs and dashboards.
Build a dashboard in a BI tool or Streamlit.
Present findings to non-technical audiences.
topics: Power BI or Tableau Public: data model, visuals, filters
Data storytelling: structure of a memo and a presentation
weeks.lab: Build a 1-page KPI dashboard from the Phase 1 retail database.

project.title: Business dashboard + memo (Phase 2 project)
project.brief: Build an interactive KPI dashboard for a business dataset (e.g. food delivery or retail chain) and a memo to the 'CEO'.
deliverables: At least one statistical test supports a recommendation

weeks.title: ML fundamentals and regression
outcomes: Explain how supervised learning works and generalises.
Train and evaluate regression models.
Always compare against a baseline.
topics: Train / validation / test splits; overfitting; bias-variance
Linear regression with gradient descent from scratch (once)
weeks.lab: Fit models of increasing complexity and plot training vs validation error.

project.title: Used-car price predictor
project.brief: Predict used-car prices (e.g. CarDekho data) and explain what drives price.
deliverables: Baseline model and at least 2 better models
Proper train / test split, no leakage
Feature effects explained for a car dealer
project.stretch: Build a simple price-check web form.

weeks.title: Classification and metrics
outcomes: Train and compare classifiers.
Choose metrics and thresholds using business costs.
Handle imbalanced classes.
topics: Choosing thresholds from costs and benefits
weeks.lab: Build a cost-based threshold chooser for a loan example.

project.title: Customer churn predictor
project.brief: Predict telecom churn and recommend which customers to target for retention.
deliverables: Threshold chosen using stated business costs
project.stretch: Estimate the profit of the retention campaign.

weeks.title: Ensembles, feature engineering and explainability
outcomes: Use random forests and gradient boosting.
Engineer features and build pipelines.
Explain models and avoid leakage.
topics: Data leakage: spotting and preventing it
weeks.lab: Competition kick-off: explore the data and submit a baseline.

project.title: In-class Kaggle-style competition (teams)
project.brief: Teams compete on a private leaderboard (e.g. credit default).
deliverables: SHAP explanation of the final model

weeks.title: Unsupervised learning and recommendations
outcomes: Segment customers with clustering.
Reduce dimensions with PCA.
Build simple recommenders.
weeks.lab: Market-basket analysis on grocery transactions.

project.title: Segmentation + product recommender
project.brief: Segment e-commerce customers and build a 'customers also bought' recommender.
project.stretch: Add a cold-start strategy for new users.

weeks.title: Time-series analysis and forecasting
outcomes: Decompose time series into trend and seasonality.
Forecast with statistical and ML methods.
Validate forecasts correctly over time.
topics: Prophet; ML forecasting with lag features
Forecast accuracy: MAE, MAPE; prediction intervals
weeks.lab: Forecast a festival-season sales spike and discuss what the model misses.

project.title: Retail demand forecast (Phase 3 project)
project.brief: Forecast store or product demand for the next 8 weeks and recommend inventory levels.

weeks.title: Text analytics, NLP and LLMs for data work
outcomes: Turn text into features and insights.
Use embeddings and LLMs to label and analyse text.
Check AI-generated labels and code for accuracy.
topics: Sentence embeddings for search and clustering
LLM APIs for labelling, extraction, summarisation
Measuring LLM label accuracy against human labels
weeks.lab: Label 100 reviews by hand and compare with an LLM's labels.

project.title: Review sentiment and topic analysis
project.brief: Analyse thousands of product or app reviews for sentiment trends and complaint topics.
deliverables: LLM vs model labels compared on a human-labelled sample
project.stretch: Build a searchable review explorer with embeddings.

weeks.title: Big data and data engineering basics
outcomes: Process data larger than memory.
Use PySpark and Spark SQL.
Explain the modern data stack.
topics: Spark SQL; joins and aggregations at scale
weeks.lab: Compare Pandas, DuckDB and PySpark on the same large file.

project.title: PySpark pipeline
project.brief: Clean and aggregate a multi-million-row dataset (e.g. NYC taxi trips or Indian railways data).
deliverables: Pipeline reads raw data and writes summary tables to Parquet
Short insights from the summary tables
project.stretch: Schedule the pipeline to run daily.

weeks.title: Deployment, monitoring, ethics and privacy
outcomes: Deploy a model as an API or app.
Track experiments and monitor for drift.
Check work for bias and privacy risks.
topics: Privacy and India's DPDP Act basics; anonymisation
weeks.lab: Run a fairness check on the Week 13 churn model across customer groups.

project.title: Deployed model with model card
project.brief: Deploy a Phase 3 model as an API or app for others to use.
deliverables: Public API or app with input validation
Fairness check across at least one group
Model card with limits and intended use
project.stretch: Add a drift report comparing new data with training data.

weeks.title: Portfolio, careers and demo day
outcomes: Package work into a job-ready portfolio.
Prepare for data science interviews.
Present a capstone to a panel.
topics: Portfolio: GitHub, Kaggle, blog posts, LinkedIn
Roles: data analyst, data scientist, ML engineer, analytics engineer
Interview prep: SQL tests, statistics questions, case studies, take-homes
weeks.lab: Final dry runs, then demo day.

capstone.summary: Teams of 2-4 take a real business or social question from raw data to a recommendation backed by analysis, a model and a dashboard, worth 35% of the final grade. Minimum requirements: real data from at least two sources stored and queried with SQL; a statistical analysis (hypothesis test, A/B test or regression) and a predictive or forecasting model that beats a baseline; an interactive dashboard or app; a written recommendation for a named decision-maker with limitations stated; and a GitHub repo with README, model card, fairness and privacy notes and a demo video. Teams may propose their own idea if it meets the minimum requirements.
ideas: UPI / card fraud detection: Which transactions should be flagged for review? (Imbalanced classification, thresholds, SHAP)
Crop yield and price forecasting: What will yield and mandi prices look like next season? (Time series, weather APIs, dashboards)
College placement analytics: What predicts placements, and what should the college change? (SQL, statistics, classification)
Air-quality forecasting: When will AQI cross unsafe levels in a city? (Time series, live data, alerts)
E-commerce personalisation: Which products should each customer segment see? (Clustering, recommenders, A/B design)
Real-estate price analytics: Is this flat fairly priced for its area? (Scraping, regression, maps)
Public transport ridership: Where and when should a city add buses or metro trips? (Big data, PySpark, forecasting)
IPL match analytics: Which strategies and player picks improve win chances? (Statistics, ML, storytelling)

milestones.item: Proposal: question, stakeholders, data sources and licences, success metric. Instructor approval required.
Data ready: collected and cleaned data in a database, data dictionary, EDA.
Analysis and model: statistical analysis or test, a model that beats a baseline, error analysis.
Deployed: dashboard or app live, model card, fairness and privacy notes.
Demo day: 10-minute presentation + 5-minute Q&A; final report, repo and demo video (up to 5 min).

assessment.component: Weekly projects (16 non-phase weeks, about 1.6% each)
Tests (timed SQL test in Week 6, statistics and ML concept quizzes)
Capstone (proposal 5%, analysis/model/dashboard 15%, final report 5%, demo day 10%)

tools: Power BI Desktop or Tableau Public
LLM API (or a local open model via Ollama)
policies: AI coding tools are allowed and encouraged; students must verify results and explain every query, test and chart they submit.
Sharing ideas is fine; copying another student's repository is not. Cite any code, tutorial or template used.
Use data you have the right to use, document licences, respect robots.txt and never publish personal data.
Late work: 10% penalty per day, up to 3 days; phase projects and demo day need prior approval to be late.
At least 80% lab attendance is required to be eligible for the capstone.
Analyses must not be presented as financial, medical or legal advice; report uncertainty and limitations honestly.
